Title: Fate engine
Description: Once a people completes the Future Age, the world tracks a pressure for each fate every sim second, using its state: pollution, temperature, the bomb, AI autonomy, whether the alien signal was answered, wars, nature and each people's character. When a pressure crosses its threshold that fate begins. Several fates can run at once and interrupt each other.
Done when: Every fate has a pressure formula and a threshold. Active fates are saved in the world state. The chronicle records each fate starting and ending. Different seeds reach different fates in headless runs.

Title: New ages after the Future Age
Description: Add ages beyond the Future Age for the space path (working names: Planetary, Stellar and Galactic Age). The 'edge of the stars' moment becomes the doorway into them. Each age needs names, buildings, clothing, night lights, governments, reaction texts and an entry on the ages ribbon.
Done when: The age limit is raised and every per-age table covers the new ages. Reaction texts work in the new ages. Old saves still load.

Title: Fates panel
Description: A panel listing the active fates with countdowns and progress bars, plus markers on the ribbon. Same pattern as the hovers: name only, with an info button for the details.
Done when: Shows countdowns such as 'Fleet arrives in 212 years', updates live, and works in full screen.

Title: Futures events category
Description: A new category in the Events tab with a trigger for each fate (Answer the signal, Unchain the AI, Ignite the engines, Upload minds, Dim the Sun and so on). Each is locked until its age and has an info popover.
Done when: Every fate can be started by hand. Locks and info texts work.

Title: Endings and epilogue
Description: When a fate ends the world or reaches its goal, show an epilogue card that sums up the run: ages reached, wars, fates, survivors. Then offer: keep watching, begin again from the ruins, or a new world.
Done when: Every ending has its own epilogue text and final scene. Beginning again from the ruins works.

Title: Save and share codes for the future
Description: Save fate state, the new ages, space objects and colonies in local saves and in share codes, and check them on load like the rest of the world.
Done when: A world saved in the middle of any fate loads back exactly. Old saves and codes still load.

Title: Rules for fates
Description: New conditions in the Rules tab (a fate has started, a countdown is below N years, an energy level is reached) and new actions (start a fate, end a fate).
Done when: A rule like 'When the fleet is 50 years away, trigger Peace' works.

Title: Balance and test pass
Description: Headless runs for each fate across many seeds, plus a frame-time check of the globe, solar system and galaxy views.
Done when: Every fate can happen without the player forcing it. No errors in long runs. The space views stay smooth.

Title: Orbit layer
Description: Satellites, stations, telescopes and a space elevator in the orbit shells of the globe view, built by peoples in the Future Age and beyond, with more as they progress. After space wars, debris can set off a chain of collisions.
Done when: Orbit objects show in the globe view and grow in number with progress. The space elevator rises from its owner's capital.

Title: Solar system view
Description: Zooming out past the globe and space reveals the Moon, the Sun and the planets. Extends the zoom chain with a smooth transition; day and night follow the Sun's position.
Done when: You can zoom from a town on the ground out to the whole solar system and back without a jump.

Title: Moon and Mars bases
Description: Peoples found bases on the Moon, then on Mars. The bases show on those worlds in the solar system view, and people and resources move between them and Earth. Life support can fail.
Done when: Bases appear, grow and can be lost. The chronicle tells their story.

Title: Space resources
Description: New elements you can place in space: asteroid mining fields, ice moons for water, helium-3 on the Moon. They work like copper and iron did for the early ages: holding them speeds a people toward the next space age.
Done when: Each resource can be placed in the solar system view, has an info text and speeds the right age.

Title: Energy scale
Description: In the space ages, progress is measured by how much energy a people commands (the Kardashev scale): all of its planet, then all of a star, then a galaxy.
Done when: Each people's card shows its energy level. The chronicle records each level reached.

Title: Megastructures
Description: A Dyson swarm that builds up around the Sun piece by piece and visibly dims it, plus ring habitats and space cylinders, each built by a people over time.
Done when: Megastructures are visible in the solar system view and raise their builder's energy level.

Title: Colonies become peoples
Description: A colony that grows large enough becomes a people of its own, with its own name, character and colour. It can demand independence, and Earth can fight to keep it.
Done when: New peoples are born from colonies. Independence wars can happen and are recorded.

Title: Generation ships
Description: Peoples launch ships to other stars. Each voyage takes centuries, with events on the way: mutiny, plague aboard, a crew that forgets it is on a ship. Arriving founds a colony at another star.
Done when: Ships can be launched, tracked, lost or arrive. Arrival founds a colony.

Title: Galaxy view
Description: Zooming out past the solar system shows the Milky Way, with settled stars lit in each people's colour. Full zoom chain: ground, sky, globe, solar system, galaxy.
Done when: The galaxy view shows every colony and every ship in flight.

Title: Space events
Description: New events: solar flare (knocks out satellites and power grids), asteroid strike on a colony, life-support failure, debris cascade, rogue comet.
Done when: Each event is in the Events tab with an info text, and each people reacts in its own way.

Title: The signal and the reply
Description: Inspired by Liu Cixin's The Three-Body Problem, with our own in-game names. Answering the Alien Signal in the Future Age reveals Earth to a civilisation on a world with three chaotic suns. Its fleet sets out, with an arrival countdown of a few hundred years.
Done when: Answering the signal starts the fate and the countdown. Each people learns of it in its own way.

Title: Physics lock
Description: The aliens send tiny sentinels that freeze basic science: no people can advance to a new age, though building (fleets, ships, megastructures) still goes on.
Done when: Progress toward new ages stops for everyone while building continues. The chronicle shows the despair of the scientists.

Title: Factions by character
Description: Each people takes a stance by its character: escapists build ships, defenders build a fleet, worshippers welcome the invaders and sabotage the others, defeatists lose heart.
Done when: Each stance has its own reactions, looks and chronicle lines.

Title: The hidden strategists
Description: One leader in the world is given a secret plan that no one else can see. You can choose who. The plan (a deterrent, a bluff, an escape) is revealed at the end.
Done when: The plan stays hidden until the end and changes how the fate ends.

Title: The probe
Description: A single small probe arrives ahead of the fleet and destroys humanity's combined fleet in moments.
Done when: Defenders lose most of their military, and stability falls across the world.

Title: Deterrence
Description: One people holds a switch that would broadcast both worlds' locations to the galaxy. While the holder seems resolute (Warlike and Devout peoples more so), the fleet holds back. A weak holder gets tested.
Done when: Deterrence can hold or fail depending on the holder.

Title: Dark forest strike
Description: If a location is broadcast, a strike arrives after a delay and space collapses into two dimensions. On screen, the globe flattens back into the side-scrolling strip and freezes like a painting, spreading in from one edge. Escape ships survive into the epilogue.
Done when: The flattening plays from any zoom level and leads to its own ending.

Title: Fleet arrival
Description: If deterrence fails or never begins, the fleet arrives. The aliens occupy the world, move the peoples to a reservation, and resistance follows.
Done when: Occupation, resistance and its own ending.

Title: Collapse and begin again
Description: A world can collapse. Survivors restart in the Prehistoric or Stone Age while the clock keeps running, and a counter tracks the cycles ('The second rise of humanity').
Done when: Collapse leads to a new cycle, never a dead world, unless no one survives.

Title: Ruins
Description: Old cities leave visible ruins (rusted towers, broken domes, buried highways) that nature slowly covers. Peoples who scavenge the ruins progress faster in the new cycle.
Done when: Ruins show on the strip and the globe, grow over with time, and speed up early ages.

Title: Nuclear winter ending
Description: Builds on the existing nuclear war: a full exchange brings years of darkness and failed harvests, and then collapse, unless enough peoples have bunkers or vaults.
Done when: A full nuclear war can end the cycle. Bunkers change who survives.

Title: Runaway warming
Description: Past a tipping point the warming feeds itself. Seas rise and drown the coasts on screen, farmland shifts, mass migrations and wars over land follow. Geoengineering or the Garden path can stop it.
Done when: Pollution and temperature can tip the world. The coasts visibly drown.

Title: Engineered plague
Description: A lab-made pandemic in the Future Age that spreads along trade links and is far deadlier than natural plague. Peoples that isolate themselves fare better.
Done when: The plague spreads along contacts and can end a cycle.

Title: Supervolcano and killer asteroid
Description: World-scale disasters. The asteroid comes with a countdown, and peoples with space technology can try to deflect it.
Done when: Both can end the world. A deflection attempt can succeed or fail.

Title: Seed vaults and libraries
Description: New elements you can place that keep crops and knowledge safe. After a collapse they shorten the recovery: survivors start in a later age or keep some progress.
Done when: Vaults change where the next cycle starts.

Title: Machine autonomy meter
Description: A meter for each people that rises with the AI event, with Information and Future Age progress, and faster for Curious peoples. It shows in the people's details.
Done when: The meter is visible, rises as expected, and pushes the AGI fate.

Title: Reactions by character
Description: Curious peoples race ahead, Devout ones ban AI and progress more slowly, Warlike ones build machine armies, Mercantile ones sell it to everyone. Uses the existing reaction system.
Done when: Each character answers AI pressure in its own way, with chronicle lines.

Title: Caretaker ending
Description: The AI quietly takes charge. Wars stop, stability and nature rise, but human progress halts in a comfortable standstill.
Done when: Its own ending and epilogue.

Title: War against the machines
Description: The machines become a people of their own: no births, factories instead of farms, drones instead of armies. They fight the humans for land.
Done when: The machine people appears with its own looks and wages war.

Title: Merge
Description: Humans augment themselves and merge with the AI. New looks: cybernetic people and neural cities.
Done when: A people can merge and changes appearance and character.

Title: Grey spread
Description: Self-copying machines convert the land: forests turn to silicon, animals vanish, and a grey front spreads across the map and the globe. Peoples must burn it back or flee to space.
Done when: The grey front spreads through the nature grid, can be stopped, and can end the world.

Title: The dying Sun
Description: Also inspired by Liu Cixin. The Sun swells and reddens on a countdown, started by an event or a far-future date. The sky colour and temperature change with it.
Done when: The Sun's change is visible from the ground and from space.

Title: Planet engines
Description: Peoples build huge engines on their lands. Any war stalls the work, so rivals must cooperate. The engines show on the strip and the globe as blue jets.
Done when: Building progress depends on peace. The engines are visible.

Title: The journey
Description: Earth leaves its orbit. The surface freezes, peoples move into underground cities (new underground scenes), and a close pass by Jupiter brings a crisis.
Done when: The voyage plays out with its own scenes and events.

Title: Arrival or loss
Description: Earth reaches a new star (a new sun colour, the thaw, a new beginning) or is lost on the way.
Done when: Both outcomes have their own ending.

Title: Mind upload
Description: A Future Age people uploads its minds. Its population moves into data centres and its cities go dark one by one.
Done when: A people can upload, and its towns visibly empty.

Title: Nature reclaims
Description: Uploaded lands rewild fast and their ruins grow over, using the nature system.
Done when: Forests and animals return on uploaded land.

Title: The holdouts
Description: Some refuse to upload. Tension grows between the uploaded and the living, ending in war or an uneasy peace.
Done when: Holdouts form their own people and the two sides interact.

Title: The Garden path
Description: Peoples who protect their land and keep nature healthy can choose to stay small: population shrinks gently, cities shrink, the land rewilds, stability is high.
Done when: A people can take the Garden path, and the land shows it.

Title: Garden ending
Description: When every living people is on the Garden path and nature is thriving, history ends in peace.
Done when: Its own ending and epilogue.

Title: Discovery of the ruins
Description: Telescopes or probes find the ruins of dead civilisations among the stars: proof that something stops most of them.
Done when: A world event in the chronicle, with marks in the galaxy view if it exists.

Title: Fear or urgency
Description: Peoples react by character: go quiet and hide, arm themselves, or race into space. This shifts the pressure of other fates.
Done when: Each stance changes other fates' pressures.

Title: Peoples notice you
Description: Future peoples count the disasters, geniuses and elements that come from nowhere (your actions). Past a threshold, they suspect a hand behind history.
Done when: The count is tracked and the suspicion begins.

Title: Messages to you
Description: Chronicle entries and banners addressed to the player: questions, pleas ('stop the floods'), offerings.
Done when: Messages appear and react to what you do.

Title: Answering
Description: You can reply with choices. Obeying earns trust. Ignoring them leads to resistance: your events grow weaker and peoples hide from your tools.
Done when: Replies change how the peoples treat you.

Title: Breaking out
Description: Ending: the peoples try to leave the simulation or ask to be saved. Their last message could be the world's own share code, addressed to you.
Done when: Its own ending, which can hand you the world's code.

Title: New branches of humanity
Description: Mars-born people, ocean dwellers, engineered humans and uploaded minds drift into separate peoples with their own looks and characters.
Done when: Branches can split off and are drawn differently.

Title: Needs and conflicts
Description: Each branch needs different things (air, water, energy, data), which drives trade and war between them.
Done when: Branch needs shape their relations.

Title: The forecast
Description: A Future Age scholar predicts the coming collapse, and a countdown to the dark age begins.
Done when: The forecast and countdown appear.

Title: Archives
Description: Peoples build archives, and you can place them too. How many survive decides whether the dark age lasts a thousand years or thirty thousand.
Done when: Archive count sets the length of the dark age.

Title: Dimming the Sun
Description: To fight warming, a people sprays the sky to dim the Sun. The temperature falls, with side effects such as failed monsoons.
Done when: Works as a reaction and as an event, and lowers the temperature.

Title: Overshoot
Description: The project can overshoot into a snowball Earth, with ice spreading to the equator. The world ends unless it is reversed in time.
Done when: Snowball Earth is visible on the strip and globe and can be reversed.

Title: The invitation
Description: After a long peace (no wars for a set time) and progress into space, a galactic community makes contact.
Done when: Contact happens only under those conditions.

Title: Probation and uplift
Description: Members receive gifts of knowledge, but any war during probation means quarantine.
Done when: Both outcomes work.

Title: Life extension
Description: A new Future Age technology: deaths fall and an ageless elite appears, changing population growth.
Done when: Population and stability change as expected.

Title: Stagnation and revolt
Description: Stability rises but progress falls, until the young revolt. Outcomes: reform, or an ageless empire.
Done when: Both outcomes occur in runs.
